Grants Management, overseen in coordination with PIN Grants Management focal point Ensures that contractual obligations are met in terms of programme deliverables; Ensures that donor rules and procedures are understood and respected by all parties, sharing information and conducting training if required on proposed systems and processes for consortium management. Internal relations: The DHoC reports directly to Head of Consortium and coordinates closely with PIN programme (programme quality, grants and partnership management) and MEAL focal points External relations: The DHoC is the main focal point for PIN as well as Consortium and Implementing Partners key programme staff, supporting them in implementation as per the award timeline, budget, set-up objectives and quality standards. Programme Development and Quality Directly responsible for quality assurance of performance measures (e.g. outcome indicators, interim milestones, and the efficacy of the overall monitoring and evaluation systems); Oversees the development and implementation of the Monitoring and Evaluation framework for the Consortium and be available to provide programmatic and monitoring guidance as needed; Develops, in coordination with the Consortium partners, US Department of State, and other stakeholders, lessons learned in the design and implementation of Consortium activities and means of responding to these. Grants Management, overseen in coordination with PIN Grants Management focal point Preparation of necessary reporting framework for Consortium and Implementation Partners, including relevant guidelines, templates and deadlines Ensuring reporting for all Consortium and Implementation Partners, according to donor and PIN requirements, is respected by all according to agreed deadlines; Collection and consolidation of narrative reports from consortium members for donor reporting; Consolidation and finalization of narrative reports, assistance with review and approval of financial reporting. Preparation of documentation necessary for any project modifications, including budget revisions, amendments, or extensions. Ensure such changes are made in close consultation with the consortium partners. Requirements: Past experience in overseeing implementation of complex, multisectoral programmes in conflict settings Demonstrated experience in donor compliance, budget monitoring, partner agreements and consolidated narrative and financial reporting. Experience in networking, partnership building and representation skills Strong knowledge of strategic project planning, management cycles, as well as knowledge management Strong organizational and documentation skills, capable of managing multiple competing deliverables Experience in early recovery and development and humanitarian programming, preferably in the region University degree in relevant field Familiarity with the conflicts’ settings Technical expertise within one of the strategic sectors will be an advantage (WASH, Shelter, Economic Recovery, Social protection and inclusion). Excellent communication, facilitation and negotiation skills, excellent spoken and written English Knowledge of Russian or Ukrainian is a preference Dynamic and result-oriented with ability to organize and plan effectively, responsible and systematic Reliable and self-reliant personality with responsible and systematic approach to work Critical analysis and problem-solving skills Ability to work in difficult conditions and under pressure Cultural sensitivity Strong ability and willingness to transfer knowledge Willing to travel within the country Reliable and self-reliant The recruitment is contingent upon confirmation of the funding. We offer: Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization in a challenging context; Starting Salary based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies, between 2900-3300 EUR; Additional allowances include: Monthly Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR; Monthly Hardship Allowance of 400 EUR; Accommodation provided by PIN/Monthly Housing Allowance up to 1000 EUR; Time off and Rest: 25 days of holiday annually; 10 sick days Rest & Recreation (R&R) policy in place: 3x 5 days of leave per year with 350 Eur lump sum allowance per each leave. Travel benefits: Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work; Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure; Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment; Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation; Health and Well-being: 24/7 Medical Support available online; Free psychological consultations available online; Professional Development: Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities, including Hostile Environment Awareness Training (HEAT); Security situation in Ukraine Humanitarian workers continue to operate throughout Ukraine, although the front-line areas are being shelled almost constantly, and main cities are being targeted with missiles and UAVs quite regularly.
